examples.ko: 우리 팀이 전반전에 두 골 리드를 잡았어요.
examples.en: Our team took a two-goal lead in the first half.

examples.ko: 기사의 리드만 읽어도 내용을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get the story just by reading the lead of the article.
We lost the lead at the last moment.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 처음부터 끝까지 리드를 놓치지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player never gave up the lead from start to finish.

examples.ko: 리드가 좋은 기사는 첫 문장부터 눈길을 끌어요.
examples.en: An article with a good lead catches your eye from the first sentence.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 리드 기타가 정말 멋있어요.
examples.en: The lead guitar in this song is really cool.

explain: 경기에서 앞서 있는 상태도 '리드', 기사의 맨 앞 문단도 '리드'라고 해요. 동사로는 '리드하다'를 쓰고, 같은 뜻의 순우리말은 '앞서다'예요. 점수를 말할 때는 '리드를 잡다', '리드를 지키다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '리드' covers being ahead in a game and the opening paragraph of a news article. The native Korean word for being ahead is '앞서다'. For scores, the set phrases are '리드를 잡다' (take the lead) and '리드를 지키다' (hold the lead). As a verb it is '리드하다'.

examples.en: The bank clerk accepted my documents.
They start accepting applications next Monday.
After my complaint was filed, I got a number ticket.
We will take applications online.
Where do I go to register?

examples.ko: 이메일로 신청했는데 접수했다는 문자가 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I applied by email, but I got no text saying it was received.

explain: 받는 쪽도, 내는 쪽도 쓰는 말이에요. 은행·병원·관공서에서 이름이나 신청을 올려 순서를 기다리는 첫 단계를 '접수'라고 해요. 서류를 내는 행동만 말할 때는 '제출하다'가 더 정확해요. '접수 완료'는 신청이 잘 들어갔다는 표시예요.
explain_en: Both the side that receives and the side that registers use it. At banks, hospitals, and offices, '접수' is the first step: you put your name or application in and wait your turn. For the act of handing in documents alone, '제출하다' is more exact. '접수 완료' means your application went through.

examples.en: Everyone stayed silent during the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 질문을 받고 한참 침묵하더니 고개를 저었어요.
examples.en: After the question, he said nothing for a while and then shook his head.
I am angry, so I am not saying anything.

examples.ko: 이럴 때는 침묵하는 게 나을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: In a case like this, saying nothing may be better.
We all ate in silence.
That person will stay silent to the end.

explain: '조용하다'는 소리가 작거나 없는 상태이고, '침묵하다'는 할 말이 있을 수 있는데도 말하지 않는 것이에요. 명사 '침묵'과 함께 '침묵을 지키다', '침묵을 깨다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: '조용하다' describes a place or person with little noise; '침묵하다' is choosing not to speak even when there may be something to say. With the noun, the usual pairs are '침묵을 지키다' (keep silent) and '침묵을 깨다' (break the silence).

examples.en: On weekends I rest at home.
I took a short break after work.
The doctor told me to rest for a week.
If you are tired, take a short rest and come back.
I listened to music while I rested.

examples.ko: 내일은 아무것도 안 하고 휴식할 거예요.
examples.en: Tomorrow I will do nothing and just rest.

explain: 대화에서는 보통 '쉬다'를 써요. '휴식하다'는 안내문이나 글에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 명사 '휴식'은 '휴식을 취하다', '휴식 시간'처럼 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: In everyday speech people usually say '쉬다'. '휴식하다' sounds stiffer and fits notices and writing. The noun works in speech too: '휴식을 취하다' (take a rest) and '휴식 시간' (break time).

examples.en: The negotiation ended before it reached the extreme.

examples.ko: 올해 날씨는 더위와 추위가 극단을 오갔어요.
examples.en: This year the weather swung between extremes of heat and cold.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 어느 한 극단으로 치우치면 안 돼요.
examples.en: On this issue, you should not lean toward either extreme.

examples.ko: 극단에 서 있는 사람들은 서로 말이 안 통해요.
examples.en: People at opposite extremes cannot talk to each other.
His claim is close to the extreme.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 감정의 극단을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: That movie shows the extremes of emotion.

explain: '극단적인', '극단적으로'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 연극을 하는 팀도 '극단'이라고 부르는데, 소리만 같고 다른 말이에요. '극단으로 치우치다', '극단까지 가다'가 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: It often appears as '극단적인' (extreme) and '극단적으로' (extremely). A theater troupe is also called '극단', a different word that only sounds the same. Common partners are '극단으로 치우치다' (lean to an extreme) and '극단까지 가다' (go to the extreme).

examples.en: The Supreme Court is in Seocho-gu, Seoul.
This case went all the way to the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court ruling came out today.
The appeal was dismissed, so they appealed to the Supreme Court.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 대법원 앞에 모인 사람들을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw on the news the people gathered in front of the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court will make the final decision.

explain: 한국의 법원은 지방법원, 고등법원, 대법원 순서로 올라가요. 대법원이 가장 높아서 여기서 나온 판결이 마지막이에요. 책임자는 '대법원장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Korean courts go up in order: '지방법원' (district court), '고등법원' (high court), then '대법원'. It is the highest, so its ruling is final. Its head is called the '대법원장' (chief justice).

examples.en: The wizard waved his staff.
A kind wizard appears in that movie.
When I was little, I wanted to become a wizard.

examples.ko: 주문을 외운 뒤에 마법사는 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: After reciting the spell, the wizard opened the door.
I went to the party in a wizard hat.
The wizard in the fairy tale helped the princess.

explain: '마법사'는 마법을 쓰는 사람을 두루 부르는 말이고, '마녀'는 여자 마법사를 가리켜요. 게임에서는 직업 이름으로도 써요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '마법을 쓰다', '마법을 걸다'예요.
explain_en: '마법사' is the general word for a person who uses magic, while '마녀' means a witch, a female one. It is also used as a class name in games. Common partners are '마법을 쓰다' (use magic) and '마법을 걸다' (cast a spell).

examples.en: I ate the muk with soy sauce seasoning on top.
Soft muk is hard to pick up with chopsticks.
My mom made muk from scratch for us.

examples.ko: 시장에서 묵 한 모를 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought one block of muk at the market.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 시원한 묵 한 그릇이 최고예요.
examples.en: On a hot day, a bowl of cool muk is the best.
You slice muk thinly with a knife.

explain: '도토리묵', '메밀묵'처럼 앞에 재료 이름이 붙어요. '묵무침', '묵사발'처럼 요리 이름에도 들어가요. 오래됐다는 뜻의 '묵다'와는 소리만 비슷하고 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: The base ingredient goes in front, as in '도토리묵' (acorn jelly) and '메밀묵' (buckwheat jelly). It also appears in dish names such as '묵무침' (seasoned muk salad) and '묵사발' (muk in cold broth). It is a different word from the verb '묵다' (to be old, to stay somewhere), which only sounds similar.

examples.en: The court summoned the witness.
The police will summon that person.
A summons letter came to my house.
I summon a new character in the game.
The National Assembly decided to summon the CEO.

examples.ko: 그 마법사는 불의 정령을 소환하려고 주문을 외웠어요.
examples.en: The wizard recited a spell to summon a fire spirit.

explain: 수사나 재판에서 사람을 불러 오게 할 때 '소환하다'를 써요. 일상에서 사람을 부를 때는 '부르다'를 써요. 게임이나 판타지에서 캐릭터를 불러낼 때도 '소환하다'를 써요.
explain_en: In investigations and trials, it is the verb for ordering someone to appear. In daily life you just use '부르다' (call). It is also used for calling up characters in games and fantasy stories.

examples.en: The smell of cake is tempting me.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 좋은 조건으로 선수를 유혹했어요.
examples.en: That company lured the player with good terms.

examples.ko: 친구가 놀러 가자고 유혹해서 숙제를 못 했어요.
examples.en: My friend tempted me to go out, so I couldn't do my homework.
Ads have many ways to entice consumers.
Be careful when someone tries to lure you with sweet words.

examples.ko: 숲의 새소리가 나를 아침 산책으로 유혹했어요.
examples.en: The birdsong in the forest lured me out for a morning walk.

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 음식, 광고, 돈도 주어가 될 수 있어요. 명사 '유혹'과 함께 '유혹에 빠지다', '유혹을 이기다'처럼 자주 써요. 나쁜 일로 끌어들일 때뿐 아니라 맛있는 음식이 마음을 끌 때도 써요.
explain_en: The subject can be a person, but also food, an ad, or money. The noun is common in '유혹에 빠지다' (fall into temptation) and '유혹을 이기다' (resist temptation). It covers pulling someone toward something bad, and also food that is hard to resist.

examples.en: My grandmother lived a long and healthy life.
What is the secret to a long life?
This drama has run for more than ten years.
I hope my parents live a very long life.
Most people in my family have lived long.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 앞으로도 장수할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think this shop will last a long time to come.

explain: 사람에게는 높여서 '장수하시다'로 써요. 프로그램이나 가게, 상품이 오래 이어질 때도 써요. 명사 '장수'는 '장수 비결', '장수 프로그램'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여요.
explain_en: For a respected person, use the honorific '장수하시다'. It is also used for shows, shops, and products that last a long time. The noun '장수' attaches before other words, as in '장수 비결' (secret of longevity) and '장수 프로그램' (long-running show).

examples.en: Only staff go in and out through this door.
Children must not enter the construction site.
He went in and out of the library every day.
You need a permit to enter.
People who come in must write their names.
The door was locked, so I could not get into the building.

explain: 안내문에는 '출입 금지', '출입문', '출입구'처럼 명사로 붙어 있어요. 말할 때는 '드나들다'도 써요. 장소를 목적어로 받아 '건물을 출입하다'라고 하거나, '에'를 붙여 '건물에 출입하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: On signs it appears inside nouns such as '출입 금지' (no entry), '출입문' (entrance door), and '출입구' (entrance). In speech, '드나들다' is also used. The place can be an object ('건물을 출입하다') or take the location particle ('건물에 출입하다').

examples.en: France is a republic without a king.
In a republic, an elected person leads the country.
India became a republic in 1950.
People gathered to found a new republic.
Korea is also a republic, so we elect a president.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 로마 공화국에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about the Roman Republic in history class.

explain: '공화국'은 나라 이름이나 정치 제도를 말할 때 나와요. '대한민국은 민주공화국이다'라는 문장이 헌법에도 있어요. 짝이 되는 말로 '왕국'을 써요.
explain_en: It appears in country names and when talking about political systems. The sentence '대한민국은 민주공화국이다' is in the constitution. The contrasting word is '왕국' (kingdom).

examples.en: Subtitles are inserted into the video.
A new word was inserted in the middle of the sentence.

examples.ko: 책 사이에 그림이 삽입된 부분이 있어요.
examples.en: Some parts of the book have pictures inserted between the text.
An ad will be inserted in the middle of the movie.
The song to be added has not been decided yet.
A table was inserted in the document, so it looks better.

explain: 넣는 사람이 주어면 '삽입하다', 들어가는 것이 주어면 '삽입되다'예요. 컴퓨터 프로그램의 '삽입' 메뉴나 영상의 '삽입곡'처럼 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '들어가다'나 '넣다'도 써요.
explain_en: If the person doing it is the subject, use '삽입하다'; if the thing going in is the subject, use '삽입되다'. You see the noun in the '삽입' (Insert) menu of software and in '삽입곡' (a song inserted into a film or drama). In daily talk, '들어가다' and '넣다' are also used.

examples.ko: 밤에 복도에서 유령을 봤다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that someone saw a ghost in the hallway at night.

examples.ko: 유령 이야기를 들으면 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: When I hear ghost stories, I cannot sleep.
Her face was as white as a ghost.

examples.ko: 이 건물에는 유령이 산다는 이야기가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a story that a ghost lives in this building.
I wore a ghost costume on Halloween.

examples.ko: 서류에만 있는 유령 회사라는 기사가 났어요.
examples.en: A news story said it is a shell company that exists only on paper.

explain: '유령'과 '귀신'은 비슷하게 쓰지만, 실제로 없거나 사람이 없는 것을 비유할 때는 '유령 회사', '유령 도시'처럼 '유령'을 써요. '유령을 보다', '유령이 나오다'처럼 동사와 함께 외워 두세요.
explain_en: '유령' and '귀신' are used similarly, but for things that do not really exist or have no people, as in '유령 회사' (shell company) and '유령 도시' (ghost town), '유령' is the word. Learn it with verbs: '유령을 보다' (see a ghost) and '유령이 나오다' (a ghost appears).

examples.en: The villagers believed in an old curse.
The witch put a curse on the prince.
The curse was lifted and the prince turned back into a person.
A cursed house appears in this movie.

examples.ko: 팀이 계속 지자 선수들은 저주 때문이라고 농담했어요.
examples.en: When the team kept losing, the players joked that it was because of a curse.

examples.ko: 그 보석에는 저주가 있다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: They say that jewel carries a curse.

explain: '저주를 걸다', '저주가 풀리다', '저주를 받다'처럼 써요. 반대되는 말은 '축복'이에요. 욕과 달리 나쁜 일이 생기기를 비는 무거운 말이에요.
explain_en: Common phrases are '저주를 걸다' (put a curse on), '저주가 풀리다' (a curse is lifted), and '저주를 받다' (be cursed). The opposite is '축복' (blessing). Unlike a swear word, it wishes bad things on someone, so it is heavy.

examples.en: He cursed the friend who betrayed him.
There is no use in cursing a bad fate.

examples.ko: 아무리 화가 나도 남을 저주하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: No matter how angry you are, you should not curse others.

examples.ko: 그 마녀는 왕자가 개구리가 되라고 저주했어요.
examples.en: The witch cursed the prince, saying he should become a frog.
I wrote a song that curses the world.

examples.ko: 일이 안 풀릴 때 자기 운을 저주한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: There was a time I cursed my own luck when things went wrong.

explain: 이야기에서는 '개구리가 되라고 저주하다'처럼 저주의 내용을 '-라고'로 이어 말하기도 해요. 사람뿐 아니라 '운명', '세상' 같은 것도 저주의 대상이 돼요. '욕하다'보다 훨씬 무거운 말이에요.
explain_en: In stories the content of the curse can follow with '-라고', as in '개구리가 되라고 저주하다' (curse someone to become a frog). Things like fate or the world can be the target too. It is a much heavier word than ordinary swearing.

examples.en: The witness testified truthfully in court.
I have to give a statement to the police about the accident.

examples.ko: 그는 자기 입장을 차분하게 진술하고 자리에 앉았어요.
examples.en: He calmly stated his position and sat down.
What he stated did not add up.

examples.ko: 피해자가 사실을 진술할 때 목소리가 떨렸어요.
examples.en: The victim's voice shook as they gave their statement.
May I state my opinion first?

explain: 경찰이나 법원에서 사실이나 생각을 말할 때 많이 써요. 명사 '진술'은 '진술을 하다', '진술이 엇갈리다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서 가볍게 말하는 것은 '말하다'예요.
explain_en: It is the verb used at police stations and in courts for stating facts or views. The noun goes in '진술을 하다' (give a statement) and '진술이 엇갈리다' (statements conflict). For casual talk, '말하다' is used instead.

examples.en: I walked slowly out of consideration for my friend.
If we are considerate of each other, there is nothing to fight about.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 다른 사람을 배려하는 편이에요.
examples.en: That person tends to always think of others.
It was a considerate thing to say, so it felt good.

examples.ko: 아이를 배려하지 않은 행동에 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I was angry at the behavior that showed no thought for the child.
I will be more considerate from now on.

explain: 명사로는 '배려가 깊다', '배려심이 있다'처럼 써요. '신경 쓰다'는 더 가볍게 쓰고, '배려하다'는 상대 입장을 생각해서 행동한다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: The noun appears in '배려가 깊다' (very considerate) and '배려심이 있다' (have a considerate heart). '신경 쓰다' (pay attention) is lighter, while '배려하다' suggests acting from the other person's point of view.

examples.en: The goods are shipped by boat.

examples.ko: 이 화물은 내일 새벽에 항구로 운송될 거예요.
examples.en: This cargo will be transported to the port early tomorrow.

examples.ko: 냉동 식품은 낮은 온도로 운송돼야 해요.
examples.en: Frozen food has to be transported at a low temperature.

examples.ko: 사고로 늦게 운송된 화물이 어제 도착했어요.
examples.en: The cargo delayed by the accident arrived yesterday.
The luggage was transported safely.

examples.ko: 해외로 운송되는 물건은 검사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Items shipped overseas have to be inspected.

explain: '운송하다'는 보내는 쪽이 주어이고, '운송되다'는 화물이나 짐이 주어일 때 써요. '배송되다'는 택배가 집까지 올 때, '운송되다'는 짐이 멀리 옮겨질 때 어울려요. 사람이 병원으로 옮겨질 때는 '이송되다'를 써요.
explain_en: '운송하다' has the sender as the subject; '운송되다' is used when the cargo or goods are the subject. '배송되다' fits a parcel arriving at your door, while '운송되다' fits goods moved over a distance. When a person is moved to a hospital, use '이송되다'.

examples.en: The doctor admitted the patient right away.

examples.ko: 부모님이 열이 높은 아이를 입원시키기로 했어요.
examples.en: The parents decided to hospitalize the child with a high fever.
The hospital admits you if your condition is serious.
His family said they had to get him admitted.

examples.ko: 할아버지를 입원시킨 뒤에 매일 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: After getting my grandfather admitted, I went to the hospital every day.

examples.ko: 입원시키지 않고 집에서 치료할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: You can also treat them at home without admitting them.

explain: '입원하다'는 자기가 병원에 들어가는 것이고, '입원시키다'는 다른 사람을 입원하게 하는 것이에요. 반대되는 말은 '퇴원하다', '퇴원시키다'예요. 주어는 보통 의사나 가족처럼 입원을 정하는 사람이에요.
explain_en: '입원하다' is entering the hospital yourself; '입원시키다' is making someone else get admitted. The opposites are '퇴원하다' and '퇴원시키다'. The subject is usually someone who decides on the admission, such as a doctor or family member.

examples.en: There is still no cure for this disease.
A new treatment drug has been developed.
The pharmacist recommended a headache medicine.
A few days after taking the medicine, I got better.
The research team is working on a cancer drug.
Be sure to read about the side effects of the medicine.

explain: 병을 고치는 약은 '치료제', 병을 막는 약이나 주사는 '예방약'이에요. 약 이름 끝에 '-제'가 붙는 말은 진통제, 소화제처럼 많아요.
explain_en: A drug that treats a disease is a '치료제'; one that prevents it is an '예방약'. Many drug names end in '-제', such as '진통제' (painkiller) and '소화제' (digestive aid).

examples.en: The two companies made the film as a joint venture.
It is a joint Korea-Japan drama.
This album is a collaboration between two singers.
They decided to set up a joint company.
This painting is a work the brothers made together.
We are looking into a joint investment.

explain: 나라나 회사가 함께 만들 때 '합작 영화', '합작 회사'처럼 앞에 붙여요. '협력'은 서로 돕는 것 전체이고, '합작'은 함께 만든 결과물이나 사업에 주로 써요.
explain_en: When countries or companies make something together, it attaches in front, as in '합작 영화' (joint film) and '합작 회사' (joint company). '협력' (cooperation) covers any kind of helping each other, while '합작' is mostly for a jointly made product or business.

examples.en: The company stores customer information in a database.
The database broke down, so the site stopped.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 단어를 데이터베이스에서 찾아 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This app finds words in a database and shows them.
I am learning how to build a database.

examples.ko: 새 데이터베이스로 옮기는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Moving to the new database took a day.
I searched for papers in the library database.

explain: 'DB'라고 줄여 쓰고, 말로는 '디비'라고 읽어요. 보통 '데이터베이스에 저장하다', '데이터베이스에서 찾다'처럼 에/에서와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is shortened to 'DB' in writing and read aloud as '디비'. It usually appears with the particles 에/에서, as in '데이터베이스에 저장하다' (save to the database) and '데이터베이스에서 찾다' (search in the database).

examples.en: The situation in the match was reversed in the last five minutes.
The mood suddenly turned around, and everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 사진의 좌우가 반전돼서 글자가 거꾸로 보여요.
examples.en: The photo is flipped left to right, so the letters look backward.
Everyone was surprised at the result in which the ranking was reversed.
The crowd cheered the moment the situation turned around.
I did not know the story would turn out like this.

explain: 명사 '반전'은 '반전 영화', '반전이 있다'처럼 이야기가 예상과 반대로 바뀔 때 써요. 능동은 '반전시키다'예요. 사진이나 화면이 좌우로 뒤집힐 때도 써요.
explain_en: The noun '반전' is used for a twist, as in '반전 영화' (twist movie) and '반전이 있다' (there is a twist). The active form is '반전시키다'. It also describes a photo or screen being flipped left to right.

examples.en: The telephone was invented in the 19th century.
With the invention of a new machine, life became easier.
They say paper was invented a very long time ago.
I do not know when this tool was invented.

examples.ko: 발명된 물건 중에서 가장 유용한 게 뭐예요?
examples.en: Of all the things invented, which is the most useful?
Many things are invented out of need.

explain: 새로 만들어 낸 물건이나 방법에 써요. 원래 있던 것을 처음 찾아낼 때는 '발견되다'를 써서 구별해요. 능동은 '발명하다', 사람은 '발명가'예요.
explain_en: It is used for newly made things and methods. For something that already existed and was found for the first time, use '발견되다' (be discovered). The active form is '발명하다' and a person who does it is a '발명가' (inventor).

examples.en: This food has its own distinctive smell.
That person talks in a way all their own.

examples.ko: 한국 문화에 특유하다고 할 만한 표현이에요.
examples.en: It's an expression you could call unique to Korean culture.
I like this cafe's distinctive atmosphere.

examples.ko: 이 식물은 이 지역에서만 자라서 이곳에 특유해요.
examples.en: This plant grows only in this region, so it is unique to this place.

examples.ko: 이 섬에는 다른 곳에 없는 특유한 풍습이 있어요.
examples.en: This island has a distinctive custom found nowhere else.

explain: '특유의 맛', '특유의 냄새'처럼 '특유의'를 명사 앞에 쓰는 형태가 더 자연스러워요. '~에 특유하다'는 어떤 곳이나 사람에게만 있다는 뜻으로 써요. 비슷한 '독특하다'는 다른 것과 다르다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: '특유의 맛' and '특유의 냄새' (its distinctive taste and smell), with '특유의' before a noun, is the most natural form. The pattern '~에 특유하다' means something found only in one place or person. The similar '독특하다' puts more weight on being different from others.

examples.en: The party primary is held next week.
He won the primary and became the candidate.
I am waiting for the primary results.
The two candidates competed fiercely in the primary.
I joined the party to take part in the primary.
The leader is chosen through a primary.

explain: '경선'은 후보를 정하는 선거이고, 그 뒤에 치르는 선거는 '본선'이라고 해요. '경선을 치르다', '경선에서 이기다'처럼 써요. 일반 투표를 말하는 '선거'와는 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: '경선' is the election to pick a candidate, and the election held afterward is the '본선'. Common phrases are '경선을 치르다' (hold a primary) and '경선에서 이기다' (win the primary). It is kept separate from '선거', the general word for an election.

examples.en: A letter came from the National Health Insurance Service.
My father works at a factory in the industrial complex.
This city has a big industrial complex.
A staff member there checked my documents.

examples.ko: 공단 근처는 아침마다 출근 버스가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many commuter buses near the industrial area every morning.
I called the agency and asked about the pension issue.

explain: '공단'은 두 가지로 쓰여요. 기관 이름 끝에 붙으면 나라 일을 하는 공공 기관이고, '공단에 다니다'처럼 지역을 말하면 공장이 모인 곳이에요. 문장에서 어느 쪽인지 보면 구별돼요.
explain_en: It has two uses. At the end of an organization name, such as '국민건강보험공단', it is a public agency doing state work. Used for a place, as in '공단에 다니다' (work at an industrial complex), it means an area where factories are clustered. The sentence tells you which one.

examples.en: The vice chairman attended the meeting.
He became vice chairman last year.
The chairman and vice chairman greeted us together.
I am the vice president of my club.
The vice chairman's speech was long.
Who is the vice president of our group?

explain: '회장' 바로 아래 자리예요. '부-'는 '부사장', '부반장'처럼 아래 직위에 붙어요. 높여서 부를 때는 '부회장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the position right below the '회장' (chairman). The prefix '부-' goes onto other titles too, like '부사장' (vice president) and '부반장' (deputy class leader). To address the person politely, say '부회장님'.

examples.en: That singer composes songs herself.
I have composed on the piano since I was little.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 생일을 위해 노래를 작곡해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend composed a song for my birthday.
Composing is hard but fun.
Who composed this song?

examples.ko: 올해 안에 앨범 전체를 작곡할 거예요.
examples.en: I will compose the whole album within this year.

explain: 곡을 만드는 건 '작곡', 가사를 쓰는 건 '작사'예요. 둘 다 하면 '작사 작곡'이라고 붙여 말해요. 곡을 만드는 사람은 '작곡가'예요.
explain_en: Making the music is '작곡' and writing the lyrics is '작사'. Someone who does both is described as '작사 작곡'. The person who writes music is a '작곡가' (composer).

examples.en: I braise mackerel together with radish.
I braised the potatoes in soy sauce.
It is a side dish of anchovies braised sweet.

examples.ko: 국물이 거의 없어질 때까지 조려야 해요.
examples.en: You have to braise it until almost no broth is left.

examples.ko: 엄마는 갈치를 조릴 때 고춧가루를 넣어요.
examples.en: When my mom braises hairtail, she adds chili powder.

examples.ko: 불을 줄이고 천천히 조리면 맛이 배요.
examples.en: If you lower the heat and braise slowly, the flavor soaks in.

explain: '생선조림', '감자조림'처럼 이 동사에서 나온 요리 이름이 많아요. 음식은 보통 '조리다'를 쓰고, 마음은 꼭 '졸이다'를 써서 '마음을 졸이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Many dish names come from this verb, such as '생선조림' and '감자조림'. For food, use '조리다'; for nervous feelings you need a different verb, '졸이다', as in '마음을 졸이다' (be on tenterhooks).

examples.en: Do not be jealous of your friend's success.
My younger sibling was jealous of me and sulked.

examples.ko: 그는 여자 친구가 다른 남자와 이야기하면 질투해요.
examples.en: He gets jealous when his girlfriend talks to another man.

examples.ko: 질투하는 마음이 들 때는 잠깐 쉬어요.
examples.en: When I feel jealous, I take a short break.
Children sometimes feel jealous of a younger sibling.
I envied them so much that I felt jealous.

explain: 연인 사이의 질투뿐 아니라 남이 가진 것이나 잘된 일을 샘낼 때도 써요. '부러워하다'는 나쁜 마음이 없을 수도 있지만 '질투하다'는 시기하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It covers jealousy between lovers, and also resentment of what others have or how well they are doing. '부러워하다' (to envy admiringly) may carry no bad feeling, while '질투하다' has a grudging tone.

examples.en: The company invited overseas buyers to the event.
The university invites a famous writer.
We will invite only family to the wedding.
I sent an invitation letter to the guests.

examples.ko: 외국에서 온 손님을 공식 만찬에 초청하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to invite a guest from abroad to the official dinner.

examples.ko: 선생님이 우리를 저녁 식사에 초청해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Our teacher invited us to dinner.

explain: 행사나 모임에 정식으로 부를 때 써요. 친구를 집에 부르는 가벼운 상황에서는 '초대하다'를 써요. 명사는 '초청장', '초청 강연'처럼 붙여요.
explain_en: It is used for formally inviting someone to an event or gathering. For a light situation, such as asking a friend to your home, use '초대하다'. The noun attaches in words like '초청장' (invitation card) and '초청 강연' (invited lecture).

examples.en: That actor was cast as the lead.
I did the audition, was cast in the drama, and was happy.

examples.ko: 캐스팅된 배우들이 첫 대본 리딩을 했어요.
examples.en: The actors who were cast did their first script reading.
She was scouted on the street and became a model.

examples.ko: 제가 캐스팅될 거라고는 생각도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I never imagined I would be cast.
I am curious about how people get cast in movies.

explain: 능동은 '캐스팅하다', 피동은 '캐스팅되다'예요. 역할 이름에는 '주인공으로'처럼 '으로'를 붙여요. 영어 cast에서 온 말이라 줄여서 명사 '캐스팅'으로도 써요.
explain_en: The active form is '캐스팅하다' and this is the passive. The role takes '으로', as in '주인공으로 캐스팅되다' (be cast as the lead). It comes from English 'cast', and the noun '캐스팅' is also used.

examples.en: The director cast a new actor.

examples.ko: 제작사는 유명한 가수를 캐스팅하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The production company wants to cast a famous singer.

examples.ko: 그 역할에 누구를 캐스팅할지 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: We are thinking about who to cast in that role.
I watched a video of the casting process.
A news story said they had cast the lead.

examples.ko: 어린이 역은 오디션 없이 캐스팅하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to cast the children's roles without an audition.

explain: '배우를 캐스팅하다'처럼 고르는 쪽이 주어예요. 뽑힌 배우 쪽에서는 '캐스팅되다'를 써요. 길에서 배우나 모델 후보를 찾는 것은 '길거리 캐스팅'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The one choosing is the subject, as in '배우를 캐스팅하다' (cast an actor). From the chosen actor's side, '캐스팅되다' is used. Finding acting or modeling talent on the street is called '길거리 캐스팅' (street casting).

examples.en: The enemy army finally declared surrender.
Okay, I give up. I lost.
When his strength ran out, he surrendered.
The news of the surrender was broadcast on the radio.
My sibling could not stand the tickling and gave in.
We will not surrender to the end.

explain: '항복하다'로 동사처럼 쓰고, 장난으로 "항복!"이라고 외치기도 해요. 비슷한 '굴복하다'는 힘이나 압력에 눌려 따르는 거고, '항복'은 싸움이나 승부에서 졌다고 인정하는 거예요.
explain_en: It is used as a verb with '하다' ('항복하다'), and people also shout '항복!' as a joke when they give up. The similar '굴복하다' (yield) is about bowing to power or pressure, while '항복' is about admitting defeat in a fight or contest.

examples.en: The mirror reflects sunlight.
The lake reflected the sky.
The window reflected light and it was dazzling.
White is a color that reflects a lot of light.

examples.ko: 산이 소리를 반사하기 때문에 메아리가 들려요.
examples.en: The mountain reflects sound, which is why you hear an echo.
Light reflected from the wall hit my face.

explain: 빛이나 소리가 되돌아가게 할 때 써요. 피동 '반사되다'도 자주 써서 '빛이 거울에 반사돼요'처럼 말해요. 몸이 저절로 반응하는 '반사 신경'이라는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when light or sound bounces back. The passive '반사되다' is also common, as in '빛이 거울에 반사돼요' (light is reflected in the mirror). The same noun appears in '반사 신경' (reflexes).

examples.en: The exchange rate fluctuates every day.
The price changed depending on the weather.
The schedule might change.
It is a day when stock prices swing widely.
If the timetable changes, I will let you know.
Please check whether the number of attendees has changed.

explain: 가격, 수치, 일정이 오르내리거나 바뀔 때 써요. 명사 '변동'은 '가격 변동', '변동이 크다'처럼 나와요. '변하다'는 성격이나 사람에도 쓰지만 '변동하다'는 주로 숫자와 상황에 써요.
explain_en: It is used when prices, numbers, or schedules go up and down or shift. The noun appears in '가격 변동' (price fluctuation) and '변동이 크다' (big swings). '변하다' (to change) can describe a person or personality, but '변동하다' is mostly for figures and situations.

examples.en: There is a fire drill this afternoon.
A fire truck passed by with its siren on.
Every building has to get a fire safety inspection.
My uncle is a fire service worker.

examples.ko: 소방 시설이 잘 갖춰져 있어서 안심이에요.
examples.en: The fire equipment is well installed, so I feel safe.

examples.ko: 화재 때문에 소방 당국이 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The fire authorities are investigating because of the fire.

explain: '소방서', '소방관', '소방차'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 불을 끄고 막는 일과 관련된 말을 만들어요. '소방' 하나만 따로 쓰는 일은 드물고 대부분 합성어 안에서 만나요.
explain_en: It attaches in front of other words, as in '소방서' (fire station), '소방관' (firefighter), and '소방차' (fire truck), to form terms about putting out and preventing fires. It rarely stands alone and is mostly met inside compounds.

examples.en: My stomach was bad, so I went to the hospital.
I ate too much and my stomach hurts.

examples.ko: 매운 음식은 위장에 부담을 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: Spicy food can put a strain on your stomach.
I skipped breakfast for a stomach exam.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차가 위장을 편안하게 해 줘요.
examples.en: Warm tea settles your stomach.

examples.ko: 아침을 안 먹으면 위장이 비어서 속이 쓰려요.
examples.en: If I skip breakfast, my stomach is empty and it burns.

explain: 위만 말할 때는 '위', 소화 기관 전체를 말할 때는 '위장'이라고 해요. 말할 때는 '속이 안 좋아요'도 많이 써요. 소리가 같은 '위장'은 정체를 숨긴다는 뜻의 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: For the stomach alone there is the shorter '위'; '위장' covers the digestive organs together. In speech, people also say '속이 안 좋아요' (my insides feel bad). A different word with the same sound, '위장' (disguise), means to hide one's identity.

examples.en: The bicycle chain came off.
I put the chain on the door and slept.
On snowy roads you put chains on the tires.
I received a chain necklace as a gift.

examples.ko: 이 커피 체인은 전국에 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: This coffee chain has stores all over the country.
The owner of the chain store manages the shop personally.

explain: 자전거 체인처럼 쇠고리를 말하기도 하고, 같은 이름의 가게가 여러 곳에 있는 '체인점'을 말하기도 해요. 가게는 '프랜차이즈'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '체인점'이라고 흔히 말해요.
explain_en: It can mean a metal chain, like a bike chain, or a group of stores under the same name, a '체인점'. Another word for such stores is '프랜차이즈', but '체인점' is the common everyday term.

examples.en: You board the plane at gate 12.
An announcement said the gate had changed.
I wait for my friend in front of the gate.
I tapped my card at the subway gate and went in.
I arrived before the boarding gate closed.
A new security gate appeared at the entrance.

explain: 공항에서는 '탑승구'와 같은 곳을 가리켜요. 역이나 건물 출입구에도 쓰는 외래어예요. '정문'이나 '입구'라고 하는 큰 문은 보통 게이트라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: At an airport, it points to the same place as '탑승구'. It is a loanword also used for station and building entrances. A main front door called '정문' or '입구' is usually not called a gate.

examples.en: He reflected on his mistake and apologized.
I look back at today and reflect on it.
He seemed to regret having lied.

examples.ko: 반성한 사람에게는 한 번 더 기회를 줘요.
examples.en: We give one more chance to a person who has reflected.
After botching the exam, I reflected on how I study.
If there is something you need to reflect on, say it honestly.

explain: '반성'은 속으로 돌아보며 잘못을 느끼는 것이고, '사과'는 상대에게 말로 하는 거예요. 학교나 직장에서 '반성하고 있어요'라는 말을 들을 수 있어요. '반성을 하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: '반성' is looking back inwardly and feeling your mistake, while '사과' (apology) is said to the other person. You may hear '반성하고 있어요' at school or work. It also works as the noun plus 하다: '반성을 하다'.
